newsitem.title: INDIA: CEPA says hopes for $5 bln India power plant deal.
newsitem.headline: CEPA says hopes for $5 bln India power plant deal.

text.p: Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) hopes to sign a $5.0 billion deal to build a 5,000-megawatt power plant in eastern India, a top company official said on Saturday.
"We hope to sign a PPA (power purchase agreement) very soon," Hopewell Holdings Ltd managing director Gordon Wu told Reuters after speaking at an international business conference in New Delhi.
Hopewell holds a 19.99 percent stake in CEPA. U.S power giant Southern Co last month completed the acquisition of an 80 percent stake in CEPA from Hopewell and other shareholders.
Wu, who remains executive chairman of CEPA, said the deal for a power plant in Orissa state had been under negotiation for two years.
"I am offering a price of 5.13 (cents per kilowatt hour) and I am not prepared to go any lower," he said.

In its 1996 annual report Hopewell said the company was negotiating the first phase of a project that would generate 10,560 MW of electricity, part of a memorandum of understanding signed with Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd.

In December 1995 an "Intent to Enter into Power Purchase Agreement Negotiations" was signed with four Indian states; under which six 660 MW power stations were to be constructed in the state of Orissa.
It was not immediately clear if the 5,000-megawatt project Wu spoke about on Saturday formed part of the earlier Orissa plans or was intended to be a new investment.
